summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of diabetes, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, Crohn’s disease, and prior right knee replacement presented with dizziness and hypotension. She was found to have leukocytosis and acute kidney injury likely secondary to hypoperfusion. Empiric antibiotics were started for possible sepsis, though blood cultures remained negative and no infectious source was confirmed. Her knee wound showed staphylococcus aureus sensitive to treatment, but no deep joint infection was found. She improved with fluid resuscitation and pressor support, which was weaned off. Her renal function gradually improved, and she did not require transfusion for anemia. She was diagnosed with a right ankle sprain after a fall, with no fracture. Medications were adjusted, including lowering valsartan and switching to metoprolol tartrate. She was discharged home with services in good condition after a four-day stay.
